newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch De Boer in retail mega-merger.
newsitem.headline: Dutch De Boer in retail mega-merger.

text.p: Dutch food wholesalers and supermarket groups De Boer Winkelbedrijven NV and Unigro NV said on Wednesday they expected to reach agreement on a full merger of the two firms.
"De Boer Unigro NV will be one of the 20 largest companies in the Netherlands," the two partners said in a statement.

The planned combination will have annual turnover of more than six billion guilders ($3.5 billion) , a workforce of more than 10,000 people and a 13 percent share in the Dutch supermarkets sector. This would make De Boer Unigro the country's second largest supermarkets chain after Ahold's Albert Heijn stores.
The two groups said the planned merger would be based on equality of both partners and would have a clearly positive effect on profits per share of the new combine.
The shares in unlisted Unigro, owned by its former chairman Eric Albada Jelgersma, will go to De Boer Winkelbedrijven in return for shares in the new venture De Boer Unigro.

This will give Unigro's present owner an initial stake in the new combination of 57 percent but this will be reduced to 49.9 percent within six months. Part of the shares will be placed with an independent foundation, De Boer and Unigro said without elaborating. ($ = 1.692 Dutch Guilders)
